Violation ID: 886114
Permit API: 081-21803
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: Lycoming Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 2020-06-04
Comments: On June 4, 2020, DEP representative Brad Kline and Justin Abbott conducted a follow up inspection at Beech Resources Premier Pad. This inspection was to follow up with the reported spill from June 2, 2020 and an inspection completed by DEP staff on June 3, 2020. The inspection on June 3, 2020 reported an area of high conductivity still remaining in the impacted area. Don Stevenson with Beech Resources and Matt Tunsing with Penn E&R were onsite. Conductivity of the excavated area of impact was screened and 1 or 2 small depressions were noticed that had a reading of 1 mS/cm to 2.5 mS/cm. The normal levels of conductivity were noted outside and downgrade of the previously delineated area of impact. So the area of impact had not changed from previous delineation. Another area was of high conductivity was noted from the inspection on June 3, 2020. That area was at the edge of the permitted MASS onsite where some off loading had taken place. That area had a small puddle of water about 3 ft. long by 2 ft. wide that was screened for conductivity. The conductivity of the water was about 7 mS/cm and the soil around the puddle was 5 mS/cm. Judging from the area that was screened for conductivity the spill appeared to be less than 5 gallons. Beech Resources said that they would collect the water from the puddle and scrape up the impact soil in that area. No new violations noted. Outstanding violations from Inspection No. 3001824 and Inspection No. 30309142 still remain.

properties.content:

Violation ID: 8249102
Permit API: 113-20487
Unconventional: Yes
County: Sullivan
Municipality: Forks Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 9/18/2025
Comments: Arrived onsite in response to a reported release of approximately 32 gallons of high conductivity fluid. While removing containment after completing the frack a puddle was noticed and was determined to have elevated conductivity. I spoke with Mike Deming onsite. At the time of inspection, it was estimated that the total release was potentially more than 1 barrel and therefore Act 2 remediation would be pursued.The impacted area is on the southern side of the pad about 75' from the southern pad edge and 25' from the eastern pad edge. The scraped area was about 18' wide by 140' long and a few inches deep. Near a freshwater storage tank there was a puddle that had a conductivity greater than 4.00 millisiemens per centimeter (mS/cm). The puddle will be removed and after the tank is removed any necessary additional scraping will be performed. When possible, the rest of the containment will be removed to screen and scrape as needed.The pad beyond the visible impacted area was dry. The eastern side of the pad runs into the rock-lined cut slope. The southern and western sides of the pad lead into the PCSM. There were no seeps noted in the downslope areas and soil conductivities were at or below 0.02 mS/cm.

Comments: On March 2, 2026, the Department conducted a Compliance Schedule Evaluation (CSE) at the former location of the MAWC well site in Springfield Township, Fayette County. Accompanying the Department during this inspection is M4 representative Brad Daugherty, who was on site upon arrival. This inspection also follows up to IR 4138371. The operator was in compliance with schedule at the time of IR 4138371, as site stabilization and/or compliance to the 12/16/2021 CO and A could not be evaluated at that time due to the heavy snow cover.A Consent Order and Agreement (CO and A) was executed between the Department and the operator on December 16, 2021. The First Modification to the COA was entered on May 1, 2025.Paragraph 3i of the 12/16/2021 CO and A states: "M4 shall immediately commence work to completely restore the Well sites upon execution of the First Amendment and complete restoration of the Well Sites by October 30, 2025, in accordance with Section 3216 of the 2012 Oil and Gas act, 58 Pa.C.S. 3216, the site restoration regulations set forth in 25 Pa. Code 78a.65, and all applicable provisions of the Clean Streams Law and the regulations promulgated thereunder. M4 shall submit form 8000 PM-OOGN0075, "Well Site Restoration Report," within sixty (60) days of restoring the Well Sites." Site restoration is to be conducted "as closely to original conditions as practicable, including restoration of original contours and capability of supporting land uses existing prior to drilling of the Well(s) by October 30, 2025, unless M4 obtains a signed and notarized written consent of the landowner to leave the Well Site in an altered state".The following was observed during the inspection:The former well site appears to have overall established additional vegetative growth. However, it has not yet achieved 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth coverage. Minor areas of exposed soil were observable on site through the temporary stabilization. Daugherty reported that the operator's contractor applied additional temporary stabilization prior to the Department's arrival to site. However, Daugherty reported that they will need to contact the operator's contractor and request that they return to cover the site more thoroughly.The Department recommends continued mulching and seeding of the former well site to establish adequate vegetative growth in the forthcoming spring.Based on observations from this inspection, the violation issued in IR 4095466 shall remain outstanding.

Comments: On 3/22/23 an incident inspection of the Veres Well Pad was conducted in response to a report of a spill reported to the Department on 3/22/23 (CTS: 370763).Background:On 3/22/23 I spoke to Keith Eighmey of Greylock to regarding a missed call from him the previous evening (3/21/23). Mr. Eighmey informed me that he had reported a spill to the Department hotline. The spill had occurred on the Veres Well Pad. According to Mr. Eighmey, an estimated 30 gallons of brine were released into an earthen containment berm. Greylock was in the process of removing the old tanks at the site to install new tanks with approved secondary containment. Two incidents resulted in the release. A small volume of brine mixed with sand and residual material was released when a manhole cover on the back of a tank was unbolted. Containment was being used at the time, but the volume of fluid mixed with the sediment overflowed out of the containment. Additionally, a vacuum truck was being used to draw down the tanks. The tank on the back of the truck was overfilled. When the suction was turned off, the excess fluid escaped back through the hose and onto the pad. I informed Mr. Eighmey that I would be coming out for a site inspection later the same day (3/22/23).The following was observed during the site inspection:-An Act 9 sign was present at the site entrance (Photo #1).-A crew was present excavating the spill area (Photo #2). According to Mr. Eighmey, they initially used ground liner containment yesterday to begin remediation efforts (Photo #3). However, Greylock has since acquired roll-off boxes and will transfer the waste that is currently on the liner into the boxes (Photo #4). -The old tanks were present and will be removed from the site (Photos #3 and #5-6).-A vacuum truck was present at the site (Photo #7).-Elevated conductivity was observed in pooled water that was slowly dripping from the sidecut of the excavated area (Photo #10).-Elevated conductivity was observed in a saturated layer of substrate below the gravel (Photos #8-9).-Elevated conductivity was not observed in the bottom of the excavated area (Photo #11). -No elevated conductivity was observed in the PCSM berms downslope of the release (Photos #12-13 and #17).-No elevated conductivity was observed at the drain outlet downslope of the release (Photos #15-16 and #17).According to Mr. Eighmey, they plan to continue excavation, install lined sump to monitor for the next few days to ensure full remediation. Additionally, Mr. Eighmey stated that Greylock is planning to follow 78a66(c)1 policy however, if further remediation efforts indicate that the release volume is greater than the initial estimate they will notify the Department and proceed with Act 2 procedures. Violations of 91.34(a), 78a57(a), 78a54, and SWMA 301 are being issued for the release.

Unconventional: No

Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 5/01/2023
Comments: This inspection was conducted in response to the notification by Cliff Easton of Consortium Energy of a crude oil release from a buried gathering line located approximately 150 feet to the south of this conventional well.Upon my arrival onsite, Cliff and I evaluated the section of roadside ditch where oil was discovered, which is within approximately ten feet of an unnamed tributary (UNT) of Turnup Run. The gathering lines for the Warrant 3410 lease are located within this ditch, therefore a failure of one of these lines is the likely culprit. Consortium has shut in all of the wells on the lease and has placed absorbent pads and peat across the ditch floor to prevent any appreciable oil from reaching the stream. At this time, only a slight emulsion is present in the UNT of Turnup Run, no sheen or free product was observed upon agitating the stream. It appears that the released crude oil remains in the soil within the ditch. Booms and pads have been placed at the inlet and near the outlet of a culvert that carries the stream across the lease road as a precaution. Consortium was coordinating with local contractors to begin excavating the contaminated soil and confirm/repair the source of the release. I advised Cliff to maintain the containment in the ditch and to regularly check the booms in the UNT of Turnup Run. If any appreciable amount of oil is discovered in the stream, please contact the Department. Cliff stated that production would not continue on the lease until the lines in this ditch are repaired or replaced.Upcoming inspections will be conducted to evaluate remediation efforts and if there is any additional impact to the UNT of Turnup Run.

An Act 9 sign is visible and located at the site entrance (photo #1).Standing water observed on the pad surface field measured for electrical conductivity (EC) at a range of ~310-332us/cm.There are 2 recently completed wells located onsite; the well permits are posted at the site entrance, however, I did not observe any tags on the wells (photo #2). 2 gas processing units (GPUs) are also located onsite (photo #3). The GPUs are held in a secondary containment structure which contained less than 10% standing water. There are 4 produced fluid tanks located onsite and stationed in secondary containment (photo #4); the containment structure contained less than 10% standing water. A dehydration unit is also noted onsite and is held in secondary containment (photo #5).Numerous temporary storage tanks are noted onsite for ongoing flow back activities, these tanks are held in secondary containment structures which retain sufficient storage capacity (photos #6 and 7). 6 upright brine storage tanks are also noted onsite but are not held in secondary containment (photo #8). 2 residual waste containers were also observed not held in secondary containment (photo #9).Perennial vegetative cover continues to grow in the areas surrounding the site (photo #10). No accelerated erosion or sedimentation was observed. A weekly erosion and sediment (E and S) inspection log is available for review and is up to date (photo #11). 1 infiltration basin serves as the site's post construction stormwater management (PCSM) control (photos #12). I departed the site at 1045 hours.

Report Details
Inspection Client: CHESAPEAKE APPALACHIA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 1/27/2021
Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 906099
Permit API: 015-22632
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Terry Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 1/27/2021
Comments: On 01/27/2021, DEP representative John Ciccone visited Chesapeake Appalachia LLC (CALLC)'s McEnaney location in response to a spill notification (CTS # 354570). The initial spill notification was called in by Danielle Schaad (CALLC) on 01/26/2021. Ms. Schaad stated that approximately 7.5 gallons of production fluid was released to the pad surface during the replacement of a production fluid tank onsite. The cause of the spill was reported to be a result of the production fluid tank cracking during the cleaning / replacement process. Mountain Energy Services and Evergreen Oilfield Solutions was called in to respond to the site and to remediate the impacted area. I arrived onsite at 1002 hours. The weather was approximately 28 degrees Fahrenheit with overcast skies. The pad surface had approximately 1 inch of snow cover present. I investigated the area of release and found that the area had been scraped and impacted soils excavated and removed from the site. It appears the extent of the excavation was adequate in removing impacted soils. There were no puddles and/or melts present around the area of release noted at the time of this investigation. The slope of the pad immediately adjacent to the area of release was inspected for potential impact. The slope was found to have no obvious indications of production fluid release. The compromised production fluid tank remained onsite within a secondary containment. It appears the region of the tank wall that cracked had been patched via a tarp and duct tape. It was noted that the tape was beginning to peel away from the tank during the time of this inspection. I called Ms. Schaad at the conclusion of my site visit. I informed Ms. Schaad of the apparent peeling of the duct tape being used to patch the cracked production fluid tank. I asked Ms. Schaad when the compromised production fluid tank would be removed from the site. Ms. Schaad stated that the tank was scheduled to be removed from the site next Wednesday (02/03). Also noted, Ms. Schaad stated that less than 1 barrel of soils were excavated from the impacted area. The release of production fluids to the pad surface is in violation of Pa. Code 78a.56(a), CSL 402(b), and SWMA 301. Due to the reported quantity of the release (7.5 gallons) and the actions taken by CALLC to remediate the area of release, violations noted are considered immediately corrected. I departed the site at 1040 hours.

Comments: This inspection is taking place in response to an operator reported spill. The incident was reported to the Department at approximately 6:33PM on 12/23/2020. Mr. Hardy from EQT was spoken to by phone on 12/24/2020. According to Mr. Hardy, the incident occurred at approximately 4:30PM on 12/23/2020. According to Mr. Hardy a pipe inside the GPU housing leaked, with approximately 5-10 gallons of fluid impacting the ground. The operator contacted SPSI to remediate. According to an email received from Mr. Hardy later in the day, impacted water was seeping from underneath the GPU into an excavated ditch. The operator has left the ditch open to act as a sump and the water will be vacuumed out as necessary. Per the operator, remediation is being conducted in accordance with 78a.66c(1), in reference to spills or releases less than 42 gallons. Based on that, the Department recommends that the operator fully remediate the site in accordance with 91.33(B), otherwise the Department requests that the operator reevaluate how much fluid was lost. Pictures taken by the operator have been attached to this inspection (Photo 1-6). Based on this inspection, violations are being issued for the discharge to the ground. The Department will schedule an on-site visit to follow up with the remediation effort as soon as possible. Pending the operator's response and the follow up inspection, further violations may be issued.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 10/05/2023 to CHESAPEAKE APPALACHIA LLC in Tuscarora Township, Bradford county. CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 8161304
Permit API: 015-23776
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Tuscarora Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 10/05/2023
Comments: On 10/5/2023, DEP representative John Rogers conducted a drilling/alteration inspection at the Chesapeake Shumhurst well site. It was 59 degrees and clear when I arrived on location. Fracking operations have ceased at the site and most of the fracking equipment has been removed from location. Two wells have been recently stimulated, adding to the one existing completed well on site. The three wells were not staged for production at the time of the inspection. Five Brine tanks and five frac tanks were staged along the east side of location. A crew was on site cleaning out the brine tanks. Twelve brine tanks and the brine offloading station secondary containment were located on the west side of location. Drilling mats were still staged east of the brine offloading station with sixteen 8'x16' mats positioned on the unprotected pad surface. I screened water and soil under the edges and within the crevices of the drilling mats and had as high as 5.61 mS conductance in the liquid and as high as 2.593 mS conductance in the mud. Due to the drilling mats, I could not screen the areas directly underneath the mats but the extent of the various crevices that demonstrated elevated conductance is an estimated 32' x 16'. I collected sample #9551-065 from an accessible water puddle at the southern edge of the mats, conductivity in the puddle field tested at 4.01 mS.There was a 6' x 2' water puddle adjacent to the north side of the twelve brine tanks secondary containment that field tested at 12.46 mS conductance. A 30' x 30' muddy area spread out from the water puddle, the muddy area had conductivity readings as high as 1.755 mS. I collected sample #9551-066 from the water puddle in this area. I screened water within the brine tank secondary containment with the result being 19.99 mS conductance; this being the upper limit of the Oakton PCTS 5There is one residual waste rolloff dumpster on site with some of the site secondary containment liner material disposed in it. The rolloff dumpster liner was not installed and the dumpster was not on secondary containment.Most of the site appeared stable and well vegetated, meeting the 70% uniform, perennial, vegetative cover. PCSM is addressed on site by a filter strip installed along the access road and one infiltration berm installed along the south edge of the site. They are adequately stabilized and functioning as designed. The release of an unknown volume of elevated conductance fluid to the pad surface is a violation of CSL 402(b). Because of the elevated conductance fluid discovered on the pad surface, the DEP recommends pursuing Act 2 due to the unknown volume of elevated conductance fluid impacting the unprotected pad surface.The DEP recommends the following:1. Install a liner into the residual waste rolloff dumpster or provide secondary containment to prevent contamination to the pad surface.2. Ensure that good housekeeping practices are used when removing the brine tanks and the secondary containment structures to prevent contamination to the pad surface.I left the site at 1115 hours.

Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event

Comments: On June 2, 2020, DEP representative Brad Kline conducted an incident inspection as a response to a reported production fluid spill at Beech Resources Premier Pad. DEP received a phone call from Don Stevenson with Beech Resources reporting a spill of around 400 gallons of production fluid from the GPU onsite. A dump line valve on the GPU recently failed and was replaced. Within the next couple days vegetation downslope from the GPU was noticed to be dead. How the production fluid was spilled is still being determined. At the time of the inspection, the operator was in the process of excavating the impacted soil. There are two strips of impacted soil, they are about equal in size. The impacted area is about 10 ft wide by 90 ft long. At the top of the slope, the excavator had dug up about 3 ft deep of soil. Soil conductivity in the right strip of dead vegetation ranged from 700 uS/cm to over range readings of the meter, which is 4,000 uS/cm. The impacted soil is still within the LOD so no production fluid left the permitted LOD. Beech Resources plans to follow the Act 2 remediation. The spill of production fluid outside of containment is a violation of the Clean Streams Law 402(b), §78a.57(a), and Solid Waste Management Act Section 301. Outstanding violations from Inspection No. 3001824 still remain.

Comments: On 02/25/2021, DEP representative John Ciccone conducted an inspection at Chesapeake Appalachia LLC’s (CALLC) Tanner & Hana location. The drilling of 3 wells commenced on location between the dates of 11/12/2020 – 11/13/2020. Drilling operations subsequently followed, were documented within inspection report # 3127696, and had recently finished. The purpose of this inspection was to document the current status of the site and to inspect the site for any indication of possible releases of regulated substances. I arrived onsite at 1335 hours. At the time of my arrival, there were 3 semi-trucks that were hauling timber matting and what appeared to be plastic corrugated pipe off location. There were an additional 11 vehicles parked around the edge of the pad, but no crew members were identified. The weather was 44 degrees with mostly sunny skies. The pad surface was mostly covered in puddles, as warm temperatures melted snow / ice cover. The containment berm and slopes around the site still had approximately 4 – 6 inches of snow cover present. The 3 newly drilled wells were inspected, and all appeared to have back pressure valves set (photo # 3). There appeared to be a thick and dark fluid within each of the well cellars (photo # 4, 5). The area immediately surrounding the wells appeared to have been recently regraded with crushed stone (photo # 6). Just west of the wells, an oily odor was noted. There appeared to be a containment liner still present on the pad surface, partially buried (photo # 7). Puddles on the pad surface around this area (noted in photo # 15) all appeared to have an oily sheen and oily odor (photo # 9, 10, 11). Black specks were present within most of the puddles, and a concentration of a dark substance was noted within a puddle (photo # 12, 13). Sample # 9544-044 was collected from a puddle along the NW edge of the site where both an oily odor and sheen were noted (photo # 14). The sample was collected for SAC 942 + Al, Br, Li analysis. The release of an unknown quantity of a regulated substance to the pad surface is in violation of CSL 402(b), SWMA 301, and 25 Pa. Code 78a.56(a). Failure to report the release of an unknown quantity of a regulated substance is in violation of 25 Pa. Code 78a.66(b)1. Violations have been cited against well permit # 015-23612. This release is referred to the DEP’s Bureau of Environmental Cleanups and Brownfields. The department recommends: 1. Dewatering the pad surface. 2. Dewatering the well cellars. 3. Removing the tarp liner noted in photo # 7 I departed the site at 1419 hours.

Comments: On 02/25/2021, DEP representative John Ciccone conducted an inspection at Chesapeake Appalachia LLC’s (CALLC) Tanner & Hana location. The drilling of 3 wells commenced on location between the dates of 11/12/2020 – 11/13/2020. Drilling operations subsequently followed, were documented within inspection report # 3127696, and had recently finished. The purpose of this inspection was to document the current status of the site and to inspect the site for any indication of possible releases of regulated substances. I arrived onsite at 1335 hours. At the time of my arrival, there were 3 semi-trucks that were hauling timber matting and what appeared to be plastic corrugated pipe off location. There were an additional 11 vehicles parked around the edge of the pad, but no crew members were identified. The weather was 44 degrees with mostly sunny skies. The pad surface was mostly covered in puddles, as warm temperatures melted snow / ice cover. The containment berm and slopes around the site still had approximately 4 – 6 inches of snow cover present. The 3 newly drilled wells were inspected, and all appeared to have back pressure valves set (photo # 3). There appeared to be a thick and dark fluid within each of the well cellars (photo # 4, 5). The area immediately surrounding the wells appeared to have been recently regraded with crushed stone (photo # 6). Just west of the wells, an oily odor was noted. There appeared to be a containment liner still present on the pad surface, partially buried (photo # 7). Puddles on the pad surface around this area (noted in photo # 15) all appeared to have an oily sheen and oily odor (photo # 9, 10, 11). Black specks were present within most of the puddles, and a concentration of a dark substance was noted within a puddle (photo # 12, 13). Sample # 9544-044 was collected from a puddle along the NW edge of the site where both an oily odor and sheen were noted (photo # 14). The sample was collected for SAC 942 + Al, Br, Li analysis. The release of an unknown quantity of a regulated substance to the pad surface is in violation of CSL 402(b), SWMA 301, and 25 Pa. Code 78a.56(a). Failure to report the release of an unknown quantity of a regulated substance is in violation of 25 Pa. Code 78a.66(b)1. Violations have been cited against well permit # 015-23612. This release is referred to the DEP’s Bureau of Environmental Cleanups and Brownfields. The department recommends: 1. Dewatering the pad surface. 2. Dewatering the well cellars. 3. Removing the tarp liner noted in photo # 7 I departed the site at 1419 hours.

Comments: On 03/11/2024, a follow up inspection was conducted at the Molek F19 well site following violations issued on 12/08/2023 (IR 3657799, Enforcement 419234). I was accompanied by Environmental Trainees Olivia Holley, Madison Raviart, and Christina Mauri (PA DEP).On 12/08/2023, violations of 102.11(a), 102.22(a)2ii, and 78.53 were issued as outstanding for the access road. Inspection from 12/28/2023 noted that the violations were still open, however the operator was in compliance with schedule. On 01/24/2024, the violations were outstanding (IR 3701625). The following was observed:Some stabilization was used along the upper portion of the access road. Several areas throughout the entire access road did not have stabilization on the open soils. I recommend that stabilization is applied (Photos 1-4). Some areas had vegetation establishing (Photos 2, 4, 5).The channel that runs along the access road did not have rip rap or stabilization. Accelerated erosion and sediment accumulation were noted within this channel, which leads to several culverts along the road (Photo 6).The upper culvert, located at 40.113707 -79.966213, had sediment accumulation within the collection point. I recommend that this is addressed (Photo 7). The culvert located at 40.11300, -79.96751 had large amounts of sediment accumulated within the collection point. The culvert was not able to be seen due to the large amount of sediment within this area (Photos 8, 9). Accelerated erosion was noted within the accumulated sediment (Photo 9). The outlet point of this culvert was covered by the roads gravel/dirt, which was causing accelerated erosion and sediment transport towards the vegetation (Photos 10-12). I recommend that this is addressed. The culvert leading to the collection box was not functioning. Sediment was accumulated and an entry point into the pipe was approximately 99% covered. Accelerated erosion and sedimentation throughout the area and vegetation were noted leading from the channel towards the collection box. There was some sediment laden water within this box. This outlets into the vegetation, where sediment accumulation was noted. The vegetation was accumulating water, which leads towards the stream within the wood line (Photos 13-19). The lower culvert outlets into a channel. Sediment accumulation was noted within the channel. I recommend that rip rap is used within this channel, as this leads directly to the stream (Photos 20, 21).The culverts along the first portion of the access road, near the site gate, were not cleaned out. Potholes along the road were not addressed. Channelization was noted leading from the potholes off of the road. The beginning of the access road, where it meets the township road, was not addressed. This area was previously displaying high levels of flow, leading onto the township road, and depositing sediment. This was noted within IR 3701625, photos 24 and 15 (Photos 22-25). The violations issued on 01/24/2024, IR 3701625, remain outstanding.

Unconventional: Yes

Comments: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted an incident inspection of Southwestern's (SWN's) Greenzweig GU-D (Reeve-Sutton) well pad located in Herrick Township, Bradford County on 11/30/2023 at 1030 hours. The weather was 38 degrees with mostly clear skies. The inspection was conducted in response to a release reported to the DEP by SWN. DEP Environmental Trainees, Erica Lutz and Evan Buck, accompanied me during the inspection.SWN reported to the DEP reporting hotline that at ~0300 hours on 11/30/2023 a release of >5 gallons of coolant (ethylene glycol) was spilled to the pad surface at their GU-D (Reeve-Sutton) site. Onsite today, SWN reported that repairs were made to the compressor unit's exhaust manifold after a small leak was noticed, which was all captured by the secondary containment skid. After repairs were complete, the reservoir was refilled with coolant and ended up overtopping the reservoir tank. The overtopping coolant was captured by the secondary containment skid but the skid ended up overtopping as well, causing the release to the pad surface. During this inspection, the majority of the impacted material had been collected but further recovery was underway. SWN reported that glycol test kits would be utilized to confirm that the entire portion of the release was recovered. See photos #1 and 2 for an overview of the release area. No evidence would suggest that any portion of the release was able to escape the gravel surface of the pad.Later in the day, SWN reported via email that the release was further calculated and reported a final release volume of 4-5 gallons of coolant was able to escape secondary containment. The final cleanup photos prior to backfilling are attached (photos #3 and 4) and were provided by the operator.Violations of the following are cited as IMMEDIATELY CORRECTED against API #015-20621:SWMA 301CSL 402(b)25 Pa. Code 78a.56aWe departed the site at 1120 hours.
